_note: The chassis board for the whole review arc. 157:2 and 157:169 draw the
same frame, so where they agree they settle the panel; boards.json also
records S5.3's five 1440 boards as `superseded:by-review-panel-156-158`,
which is this family.
Probe, not the live app: every state here needs a review round, an invited
client, comments, and — for the Detached group — the orphan announcement
only the canvas CommentLayer makes. `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_COLLAB` is off in
production, so no click in the standalone editor reaches any of it. The
probe mounts the REAL ReviewTab and stubs the tRPC transport underneath,
so ReviewService's own mapping still runs.
WHAT MOVED, and why the board won:
· CommentRow was 14/20 with a WRAPPING body and its per-row actions on a
fourth line — a ~90px row against component 17:40's 64 ('64h' is the
component's own description). Body is now 13/20 clipped to one line
(`title` keeps the full text), meta 12/18 Inter (it was the mono/11
ROW_META_CLASS), body gap 2, padding 16/12/10, fill bg-card. The
actions kept their capability and moved to the row's trailing slot.
· The progress block and the sent line were one padded column; 157:8 and
157:12 are a 44 block and a 28 block. The track is fixed at 140 rather
than flex-1 — the count is mono and tabular exactly so it does not
move, which a flexible track would undo. The count was 12px, board 11/16.
· The section band's count is now mono (component 16:16: 'the
right-aligned count is mono so the numbers do not jitter'), and the
band label carries its 16px line box and 0.5px tracking.
· Compare was a default 40-tall Button in a 53-tall bordered foot;
229:1090 is the 28 dense secondary in a 40 block with no rule above it.
· The round strip's label was ink-soft; 157:46 is ink.
NOT anchored, and why:
157:2 root — the board fills it bg-panel and rules it gray-100. The
panel's own root is transparent and takes white from the shell slot it
mounts into (the 164:22 ruling, issues-filtered).
157:10 progress FILL — `w-[95px]` of a 140 track is 68%, on a board whose
own label says 9 of 12 (75%). That is sample data, and the width is the
only property on the node, so the fill cannot be anchored at all.
157:14 Detached band (h32) and 157:39 Resolved band (h32) — both are
one-off frames on this board; the Section header COMPONENT drawn twice
beside them (220:855, 220:859) is 28, and so is the code. A component
instance outranks a hand-drawn copy of itself.
157:54/55/56/57 Detached list — the same row drawn by hand rather than as
Comment row. Its body and note carry `w-[135px]` / `w-[178px]`, which
are Figma text-frame widths inside a 280 column, not layout. Its meta is
11/16 where the component beside it is 12/18.
157:44 Round history — 70 tall for a single 18px line sitting at top 8.
Both boards draw it; neither explains 44px of empty tint. Its label
(157:46) IS anchored. See the report's Found-not-fixed.
157:51 Re-send block (h44) — the code also renders `Revoke link` under
the primary, which 158:105/158:162 require and this board omits.
229:1092 Re-send button — the board fills it `--flowbite/blue/600`
(#1C64F2). The product has ONE accent, `#1A56DB` (DESIGN.md §Color,
root CLAUDE.md), which the S5.4 gate boards in this same arc use for
their primary. A single board does not re-settle the accent, so only
its LABEL (I229:1092;9:19) is anchored.
I228:1017;17:37 Comment body column — filling it bg-card would put an
opaque white block over the row's hover tint.
COPY (`check-board-copy`, advisory): every lead on this surface is either
tokenisation or already recorded above.
"⚠ detached" vs "detached" — the board sets a warning GLYPH in the text;
the code renders a lucide AlertCircle beside it. Same mark, different
carrier, and the icon is the one that can be hidden from a screen reader.
"reattach" / "resolve" — product renders, no board draws. True, named
above: the boards draw no per-row control, and the arc does not delete a
working capability to match a drawing. They moved to the row's trailing
slot so the row is still the board's 64.
"# of #", "sara · client · home · #d", "round # of #" — the live line is
several text nodes and the checker compares whole nodes. The strings are
in `measured/review-panel-detached-present.json` under `rendered`.
